## Historical audit — S0159

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C2/test/commons_199974832/trajectory.jsonl`, JSONL line 28, student `model_request`, visible characters **[0,419000) of 452011**. The line contains a replayed conversation; the reference and renders themselves are not visible in this audit.

| Evidence in visible line 28 | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| System instruction and initial student program, [0,419000) | The task was single-photo reconstruction in SceneAct/Blender, with separate editable objects and no reference-image projection. The student interpreted the scene as a stocked woodworking shop. Code constructs walls, a window, shelves, bench, many planes, kettle, bottle, vise and bowl. These are evidence of modeled objects, not independent verification of the photograph. |
| Initial program and step 1 runner result, [0,419000) | The program groups multipart objects, including a plane’s body, blade and handles and a kettle’s body, spout and handle. It assigns procedural wood noise/bump and metallic finishes, camera parameters and three area lights. Grouping and coordinates do not prove physical contact or correct pose. The runner reports `ok: true`, completed rendering and a saved image. |
| Student’s `BEST 1` visual audit, [0,419000) | The student reports a large cuboid obscuring the tabletop, excessive side-shelf extent and washed-out materials. It hypothesizes a Boolean-bowl problem, local shelf geometry and excessive illumination, respectively; it keeps the camera fixed. These are student visual judgments and diagnoses, not independently verified findings. |
| Revision and step 2 result, [0,419000) | Following the explicit user request to implement its audit, the student replaced the Boolean bowl with a segmented basin, shortened both side shelves and reduced emitter powers. The runner reports step 2 `ok: true` and a saved render. Actual image improvement and connections remain unverified here. |
| Student’s `BEST 2` audit and next program, [0,419000) | The student reports pale materials, regular shelf silhouettes and empty foreground strips. It changes shader initialization and darkening, varies plane shapes/angles and adds clutter while retaining camera and lighting. Step 3’s result begins with `ok: true`, but its long log is cut off in this chunk; completion, final selection and final visual quality are not visible. |

**Input and autonomy.** The visible user/runner supplied the task, successful-run feedback, image references and requests for audits and revisions. The student independently generated the diagnoses and corrections. No separate teacher diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption is visible; the student’s adoption of its *own* audit is directly evidenced by the next program. Availability of image paths is not independent access to those images by this auditor.

**Outcome and lessons.** Steps 1 and 2 show formal execution/render success, not proven scene fidelity. Step 3 has a reported success flag but a truncated log; the overall outcome is **unknown**, not an established algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption. Transferably, separating local geometry, camera and lighting hypotheses and checking a rendered revision can make debugging more interpretable. The suspected Boolean cutter and shader-color causes are task-specific, unresolved hypotheses; visual similarity, object poses, material appearance, shelf support and final submission require evidence outside this visible chunk.
